\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{حاملہ} (hāmilā)}{حاملہ (hāmilā)}]{\ur{حاملہ} (hāmilā) — pregnant}

\label{lesson:UR-C483-hamila}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to have (something) cut, then the Urdu for to trim.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{حاملہ}}
\textbf{\ur{حاملہ}} — \emph{hāmilā} — \textquotedblleft{}pregnant\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{میری} \ur{بہن} \ur{حاملہ} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{merī bahan hāmilā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My sister is pregnant.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{حاملہ}} (\emph{hāmilā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ḥāmila}, \textquotedblleft{}carrying\textquotedblright{}, and so \textquotedblleft{}pregnant\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hāmilā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hāmilā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{merī bahan hāmilā hai.} — My sister is pregnant.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to have (something) cut, then the Urdu for to trim, then say \emph{hāmilā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{حاملہ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Pregnant\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{جننا} (jannā)}{جننا (jannā)}]{\ur{جننا} (jannā) — to give birth to}

\label{lesson:UR-C483-janna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to trim, then the Urdu for pregnant.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{جننا}}
\textbf{\ur{جننا}} — \emph{jannā} — \textquotedblleft{}to give birth to\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بلی} \ur{نے} \ur{چار} \ur{بچے} \ur{جنے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{billī ne chār bachche jane.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The cat had four kittens.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{دو} \ur{بچے} \ur{جنے}, \emph{us ne do bachche jane}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{جننا}} (\emph{jannā}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{janáyati}, \textquotedblleft{}causes to be born, begets\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 5102).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to trim, then the Urdu for pregnant, then say \emph{jannā} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پیدا} \ur{ہونا} (paidā honā)}{پیدا ہونا (paidā honā)}]{\ur{پیدا} \ur{ہونا} (paidā honā) — to be born}

\label{lesson:UR-C483-paida-hona}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for pregnant, then the Urdu for to give birth to.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پیدا} \ur{ہونا}}
\textbf{\ur{پیدا} \ur{ہونا}} — \emph{paidā honā} — \textquotedblleft{}to be born\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{میرا} \ur{بھائی} \ur{جنوری} \ur{میں} \ur{پیدا} \ur{ہوا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{merā bhāī janvarī meṅ paidā huā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother was born in January.
\end{quote}

Past (she …): \ur{وہ} \ur{لاہور} \ur{میں} \ur{پیدا} \ur{ہوئی}, \emph{voh lāhaur meṅ paidā huī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پیدا} \ur{ہونا}} (\emph{paidā honā}) is built from \textbf{\ur{پیدا}}, usually traced to Persian \emph{paidā}, \textquotedblleft{}appearing, born\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ur{ہونا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to be\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پیدائش} (paidāish)}{پیدائش (paidāish)}]{\ur{پیدائش} (paidāish) — birth}

\label{lesson:UR-C483-paidaish}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to give birth to, then the Urdu for to be born.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پیدائش}}
\textbf{\ur{پیدائش}} — \emph{paidāish} — \textquotedblleft{}birth\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بیٹی} \ur{کی} \ur{پیدائش} \ur{پر} \ur{سب} \ur{خوش} \ur{تھے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{beṭī kī paidāish par sab khush the.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Everyone was happy when the daughter was born.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پیدائش}} (\emph{paidāish}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{paidāish}, \textquotedblleft{}birth\textquotedblright{}, the noun of \emph{paidā}, \textquotedblleft{}born\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to give birth to, then the Urdu for to be born, then say \emph{paidāish} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{نومولود} (naumaulūd)}{نومولود (naumaulūd)}]{\ur{نومولود} (naumaulūd) — a newborn}

\label{lesson:UR-C483-naumaulud}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to be born, then the Urdu for birth.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{نومولود}}
\textbf{\ur{نومولود}} — \emph{naumaulūd} — \textquotedblleft{}a newborn\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{نومولود} \ur{بچہ} \ur{دن} \ur{بھر} \ur{سوتا} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{naumaulūd bachchā din bhar sotā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A newborn baby sleeps all day long.
\end{quote}

Masculine or feminine, by the person meant.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{نومولود}} (\emph{naumaulūd}) is built from Persian \emph{nau}, \textquotedblleft{}new\textquotedblright{}, and Arabic \emph{maulūd}, \textquotedblleft{}born\textquotedblright{}, the way it is usually traced.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{naumaulūd}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{naumaulūd bachchā din bhar sotā hai.} — A newborn baby sleeps all day long.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to be born, then the Urdu for birth, then say \emph{naumaulūd} again
\end{itemize}
